newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon gets $183.5 mln in loans for electricity.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon gets $183.5 mln in loans for electricity.

text.p: International banks and financial institutions have loaned Lebanon a total of $183.5 million to finance the construction of a high-voltage electricity network, newspapers said on Saturday.

They said the agreements were signed in Beirut on Friday between the head of the Lebanese government's reconstruction agency, the Council for Development and Reconstruction, and representatives of the banks and institutions.

"The contracts...for a total of about $183.52 million are an essential part of the government's plan to raise the level of electricity production and its distribution on all Lebanese territories," CDR head Nabil al-Jisr told reporters after the agreements were finalised.
The projects are to be finished within 18 and 30 months.

The first loan deal was signed with France's Banque Paribas for $65.62 million and the London branch of the same bank for $20.08 million to finance the building of four high-voltage conversion stations in Beirut and surrounding areas.
The stations will to be set up by France's Schneider Electric S.A.
A second loan deal for $32.94 million was signed with a number of European banks and institutions. The money will finance the establishment of three conversion stations in south and east Lebanon.

A third loan for a total of $64.88 million to fund underground cables in Beirut was signed. The money will be provided mainly by the European Investment Bank, Banque Indosuez, and a small part will come from local lenders.
